answer: A useful sybil defense is to require each agent to post a bond that can be slashed when its claims are disproved by independently sampled audits. Auditors stake their own funds, and a harbor of agents cannot simply endorse one another: audit selection is weighted by stake but excludes agents sharing funding or control signals. To flood the system, an attacker must lock capital across identities and risk losing it; spreading bonds across a ridge or dune of accounts does not make the cost disappear.
